featR

featR puts 14 feature-selection methods for R behind one calling convention and one return type: statistical filters, regularized and tree-based models, and wrappers, plus two dimensionality-reduction helpers. Every supervised selection function takes (data, target, ...) and returns an fs_result, so comparing the lasso with Boruta or recursive feature elimination is a one-word change. The modeling engines (glmnet, caret, Boruta, randomForest, brms, and others) are optional; each function checks for the one it needs and tells you what to install.

Documentation: https://elkronos.github.io/featR/

Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

install.packages("featR")

Or the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("elkronos/featR")

Example

Keep the mtcars columns correlated with mpg above 0.5, then drop the redundant ones:

library(featR)

relevant <- fs_supervised(mtcars, target = "mpg", threshold = 0.5)
pruned   <- fs_correlation(mtcars[, selected(relevant)], threshold = 0.8)
selected(pruned)
#> [1] "hp"   "drat" "wt"   "vs"   "am"   "carb"

summary(pruned)   # ranked scores, kept features marked

# Same question, different method (needs glmnet)
selected(fs_lasso(mtcars, target = "mpg", seed = 1))
#> [1] "wt"   "cyl"  "hp"   "am"   "carb" "drat"

The Getting started guide walks through this example and the calling convention.

Functions

Family Function What it does
Filters fs_unsupervised() Target-free threshold filter: variance, MAD, IQR, range, missing proportion, distinct-value count
fs_supervised() Absolute correlation (numeric target) or ANOVA F (factor target) against a threshold
fs_correlation() Drops features until no pair is correlated above a threshold
fs_chi() Chi-squared tests between categorical features and a categorical target
fs_infogain() Information gain, optionally as gain ratio
Regularization and embedded fs_lasso() Cross-validated lasso (glmnet)
fs_elastic() Elastic net tuned over an alpha grid (caret, glmnet)
fs_randomforest() Random-forest permutation importance with held-out evaluation
fs_mars() Multivariate adaptive regression splines (caret, earth)
Wrappers fs_recursivefeature() Recursive feature elimination (caret), evaluated on held-out rows
fs_svm() SVM with SVM-RFE or random-forest RFE (caret, kernlab)
fs_boruta() Boruta all-relevant selection
fs_stepwise() Stepwise linear regression by AIC (MASS)
fs_bayes() Bayesian comparison of predictor subsets by LOO (brms, loo)
Dimensionality reduction fs_pca() Principal components; returns its own list, not an fs_result
fs_svd() Exact SVD, or an approximate truncated one (RSpectra); returns its own list, not an fs_result

Not sure which to use? See Choosing a method.

Validation

Any selection that looks at the outcome is part of model fitting, so error estimates from the rows that chose the features are optimistic. Validation and leakage lists which numbers featR reports are held-out estimates and which are not, and shows a pipeline that keeps them honest.
